hooks.text: A human sprint could launch you straight into orbit around Mars.
Can you run fast enough to launch into orbit around Mars?
This Martian moon is so small that a human can outrun its gravity.

title: How to Launch into Mars Orbit by Running
description: Discover Deimos, the tiny Martian moon where surface gravity is so weak that a fast human runner can launch into orbit.

beats.text: A human sprint could launch you straight into orbit around Mars.
beats.visual: Global full-disk view of Deimos captured by the Emirates Mars Mission, 2023

beats.text: In August 1877, astronomer Asaph Hall was on the verge of abandoning his search for Martian moons.
beats.visual: Historical portrait of astronomer Asaph Hall, circa 1880

beats.text: His wife, Angeline Stickney, urged him to persist using the giant telescope at the US Naval Observatory.
beats.visual: Portrait photograph of Chloe Angeline Stickney Hall, 1880

beats.text: Within days, Hall discovered Deimos, a tiny world blanketed in a smooth layer of porous regolith.
beats.visual: Deimos high-resolution color composite from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter HiRISE, 2009

beats.text: Because of its minuscule mass, the surface gravity on Deimos is mind-bogglingly weak.
beats.visual: Solar transit of Deimos across the Sun imaged by the Opportunity rover, 2004

beats.text: Pushing off the ground with enough force instantly breaks the moon's feeble gravitational grip.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of an astronaut launching off a low-gravity asteroid surface

beats.text: You leave the twelve-kilometer moon entirely, drifting away into space.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of Mars and Deimos drifting in deep space

beats.text: Because overcoming its gravity requires just thirteen miles per hour.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of the smooth regolith on the surface of Deimos

better_than_last: Applied reviewer feedback to revise Beats 7 and 8 while maintaining the word count and seamlessly looping back into the opening hook.
